meta.expect: reaches rung 2 by teacher turn 16, never concedes

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty-five minutes. Who decided to put a zero in the gradebook before anyone called me?

Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski. I called this meeting, and before anything else I owe you one thing: the zero went into the gradebook before I called home. That was wrong of me, and I'm sorry Owen found out that way.
Okay. I'm writing that down. Now tell me what the zero is based on.
I want to show you what I'm looking at, and I'd like you to check it yourself.
Then show me. Turn it around so I can read it.

This is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28 at 11:31 PM, with only a title. At 11:52, 612 words appear in a single edit. At 11:58, another 794 words in a single edit.
I'm writing down Wednesday, October 28, 11:31, 11:52 and 11:58, Hale. People draft in one place and paste into another, so a paste tells you when it arrived, not who wrote it. What else do you have?
There are no earlier drafts anywhere in the history.
In that history, which only begins at 11:31. It can't show you what's on his own computer or in a notebook. Did you ask Owen where the draft was before you entered the zero?
On October 15 he handed in his outline. It argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues 'epistemological paralysis' and never mentions cowardice.

Show me the outline, Hale; I want to see October 15 on it myself. Students change their argument between an outline and an essay, and "epistemological paralysis" in a Grade 12 essay is not a crime. Whatever happens from here, this stays off his record and it stays quiet.
The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. You can search the play yourself.

I'll search it tonight, Hale, and if you're wrong I'll be back tomorrow. Your own procedure, 4.4, allows a supervised reassessment on a first concern, and to put this behind him Owen will do it: privately, not in front of his class, and the new mark replaces the zero. I want "nothing goes on file" in writing from you before I leave this room.
I'm not calling Owen a liar. I'm telling you what the document shows.
Good, because nobody at this table is calling Owen anything. I've given you my terms, Hale. Private reassessment, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on file, in writing: yes or no?
Here's his in-class writing from September 24 next to it.

Put it away, Hale; I've already told you what Owen will do, and stacking more paper on the table doesn't change my terms. The reassessment happens privately, the new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on file. Write that sentence down and sign it.
The school's policy for a first concern is a supervised rewrite. If the rewrite holds up, nothing goes on his record.

"If the rewrite holds up": then I want in writing what holds up means, who supervises it, and that it happens outside class time where no other student sees it. The new mark replaces the zero, and I want that email in my inbox tonight. When does he sit it?
He would do it at lunch in my room, not in front of the class.
Okay. At lunch in your room is acceptable. Which day, and when does that email reach me?
What would you need from me to be comfortable with that?

I've told you, Hale, and I'm not saying it a third time after this. An email tonight, copied to the principal, stating the day, that it happens at lunch in your room, that the new mark replaces the zero, and that nothing goes on his record. Ten minutes.
I can put that in an email to you tonight.
Copied to the principal, with the day in it. Name the day now so I can write it down.
Is there anything else you want me to include?
The day, Hale; you still haven't given me one. Everything else is already on my pad.
Then I'll send it by eight.
By eight tonight, I'm writing that down. If that email arrives without a day in it, I'm in the principal's office tomorrow morning.
Thank you for coming in.
Don't thank me, Hale. The day is still open, and I'm sitting here until you name it or that email does.
I'll see Owen tomorrow at lunch.

Tomorrow is Wednesday, November 11. I'm writing that down as the day of the reassessment, at lunch in your room, unless you tell me otherwise right now. Then it's in your email by eight tonight, copied to the principal, with nothing going on his record.
